messages.subject: Re: Deducer ver 0.3-0
messages.body_plain:
Eric,

Version 0.3-0 is the development version of Deducer and will be released when the next version of rJava is put on CRAN. Version 0.2-3 has the variable SingleVariableWidget, which I think is what you are looking for. You can see a full list of available widgets in the manual: http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.BuildingDialogsInR

Here is a simple example using SingleVariableWidget:

dia <- new(SimpleRDialog)
setSize(dia,500,500)
vs <- new(VariableSelectorWidget)
addComponent(dia,vs,1,400,800,1)
sv <- new(SingleVariableWidget,"SingleVariableWidget",vs)
addComponent(dia,sv,400,900,550,450)
dia$run()

Ian

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tal,

I'm believe that your problem is lower level than Deducer, as Deducer doesn't have any (non-Java) compiled code. It looks like there is a problem with your C compiler. Did you install R from the source code, or any packages? If so, go to http://www.murdoch-sutherland.com/Rtools/ and make sure that you are compiling with gcc.

As a wild stab in the dark, here is what might be happening. Since R works okay for you, I'm guessing that you installed it as a binary. If you install rJava from source (i.e. with something like install.packages("rJava",type="source"), and your compiler changed the floating point precision, R and rJava wouldn't be able talk to each other reliably. Reinstall Deducer's dependencies using the binaries on CRAN.

This error indicates a problem with your set-up unrelated to Deducer, though I will help you so far as I can.

Ian

Hi Ian,

Quick questions....

I need to go back and read the Deducer instructions/manual, but is it
possible to quickly generate regression numbers?

What I need to do is estimate a set of frequency parameters for bat
calls based on the size of each bat species.

frequencies and the size of the bats.

SppC        39            42

SppE        22.4            ?
SppF        41.3           38.7

am working with a data set from Mexico with many unconfirmed species
acoustically.

What I would like to be able to do is enter the size of the bats using
the forearm (FA) size in mm and the characteristic frequency (Fc) all
known species.

Then enter the FA of those species we do not yet have calls for and have
a regression number estimate for what these Fcs may be.

How can I do this in Deducer easily.

I tired directly in R by my lines of code were not correct and syntax
was really not working.

Thanks for any suggestions.

Bruce

messages.subject: Re: Deducer query
messages.body_plain:
Bruce,
You can do this by exporting the predicted values from a simple linear regression.

1. Enter in all your data, with NA in the places where you don't have FC values.
2. go to analysis->linear model, and add FC as the outcome, and FA as a numeric predictor. Click continue
3. In the model builder, add FA to the model. click continue
4. In the model explorer, click Export, and check 'predicted'. This will give you model based estimates of your data. Click run.
5. There should now be a new variable called 'predicted' in your data, which gives the best guess of FC based on FA

Ian
